subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this shared residual durable-state schema and shared-handle lease model, or should the identified facts remain within existing owner-specific state APIs?
rationale: The patch is a new cross-owner persistence foundation rather than a repair to an established product contract, and the linked RFC that defines its boundary is still open without maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Pause for RFC sponsorship
options.body: Do not merge this implementation until a maintainer explicitly accepts or narrows the residual durable-core boundary in the linked RFC.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core seam
options.body: Approve a reduced, named cross-owner invariant and request focused ownership, migration, and caller-contract review before merging this foundation.

options.title: Keep facts owner-specific
options.body: Reject the shared layer and route any concrete missing behavior to the existing task, flow, subagent, delivery, session, or restart owner.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC sponsorship
recommendation.body: Do not merge this implementation until a maintainer explicitly accepts or narrows the residual durable-core boundary in the linked RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposal and current implementation and are the best available routing contact in the supplied history, though the final product decision requires a repository maintainer.
